# Tucson Monthly & Seasonal Reviews for 2026
**July 2026 monthly review for Tucson** **11th warmest****&15th driest on record** The July outlook from the Climate Prediction Center for Tucson favored**above**-n ormal monthly mean temperatures (39% **above** vs 28% below) and **above**-normal total precipitation amounts (40% **above**vs 27% below). The month kicked off with near-normal high temperatures of 101° & 102° and unseasonably cool low temperatures of 68° & 69°. This marked the first time since 2004 that the month opened with three consecutive sub-70° low temperatures. Above-normal high temperatures were in the 105° to 109° range from the 5th through the 10th with Excessive Heat Warnings in effect on the 7th & 8th. Moisture increase on the 7th led to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms across mostly the eastern and southern portions of the metro area. Rainfall amounts were mostly less than 0.15" with isolated spots up to 0.50". On the 8th, storms were mostly near the Catalina and Rincon mountains with isolated rainfall totals between 0.50" and 1.00" between Sabino Canyon and the Tanque Verde area. The 9th and 10th were dry. An active monsoon pattern took hold from the 11th through the 21st, delivering relief from the heat. From the 16th to the 22nd, Tucson enjoyed 7 consecutive days with high temperatures below 100°, the longest such streak in July since 2018 (which had 8). Below is a recap of the most notable days during this time period. * **11th:** Severe Thunderstorm Watch was issued by the Storm Prediction Center (SPC). Numerous severe thunderstorm warnings were issued as a line of severe thunderstorms swept across the metro area from east to west. Wind gusts of 55 to 70 mph were recorded with Davis-Monthan Air Force Base recording a wind gust of 81 mph. Rainfall was mostly less than a half an inch with localized amounts over one inch. Localized areas of flash flooding were also reported.

# Tucson Monthly & Seasonal Reviews for 2026
* **12th:** Severe Thunderstorm Watch was issued by the Storm Prediction Center (SPC). Another round of severe thunderstorms swept across the metro area from east to west. Wind gusts of 55 to 70 mph were recorded. Rainfall amounts were a little less than the 11th, mostly less than four-tenths, but there were localized amounts over one inch. * **13th:** Following morning light showers, scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall, localized flash flooding, and isolated winds gusts up to 60 mph. * **16th:** Scattered showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rain and localized areas of flash flooding. Rainfall totals in the foothills near Sabino Canyon ranged from one to two inches. Hot temperatures returned to the area during the last 9 days of the month. Highs consistently ranged from 105° to 109° while overnight lows hovered between 80° and 84°. Extreme Heat Warnings were in effect from the 23rd to 25th, 30th, and 31st. The monthly average temperature of 89.8° ranks as the **11th warmest** July on record, tied with 2025. Temperature extremes range from a high of 109° on the 24th to a low of 68° on the 1st & 2nd. Four record warm daily low temperatures were set during the month (84° on 24th; 83° on 27th; 84° on 30th; & 83° on 31st). Rainfall totals across the Tucson metro area varied considerably, based on data from rainlog.org, CoCoRaHS, andPima County Regional Flood Control District gages. General totals range from 0.40" to 2.00" with isolated areas recording 2.50" to 4.00". At the Tucson International Airport, the official recording spot in Tucson, only 0.70" was recorded. This is 1.51"**below** normal and ranks as the 11th driest on record. The image below is courtesy of the Pima County Regional Flood Control District.

**July 2026 stats****Month****Normal****Departure****Historical Ranking** Average high temperature 102.3°100.2°**+ 2.1°****16th warmest** Average low temperature 77.3°76.3°**+ 1.0°****9th warmest** Average temperature 89.8°88.2°**+ 1.6°****T-11th warmest** Days with highs 100° or hotter 22 19+ 3 T-24th most Days with highs 105° or hotter 14 9+ 5 T-8th most Days with highs 110° or hotter 0 1- 1 98th July with 0 Rainfall 0.70"2.21"**- 1.51"****T-15th driest** Period of record: 132 years (1895-2026) * * * **Monsoon 2026 rainfall** Monsoon 2026 is off to a slow start with 1.75" recorded at the Tucson International Airport through July which ranks as the **46th driest** first 47 days on record. As is typical for summer thunderstorms, rainfall totals across the Tucson metro area vary widely, ranging between 0.50" to 2.50" with isolated locations recording 3.00" to 5.00". * * * **2026** The average yearly temperature of 74.0° through the end of July shatters the previous warmest January to July period by **1.5°** (72.5° in 2018). Rainfall at the Tucson International Airport, the official location in Tucson, has fallen below normal due the rather dry July. The total of 4.26" is nearly nine-tenths of an inch **below** normal and ranks as the **42nd driest** January through July period on record.
